headline: Trump tells FT US has 'no immediate plans' to strike Iran but is 'locked and loaded'
dek: Trump told the FT the US has no immediate plans for new strikes on Iran: 'I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it.' He said 'We seem to be getting everything we want,' called the situation 'a brilliant situation,' said more oil is now…
sources: Financial Times (six-minute telephone interview with President Donald Trump, Nov 3), relayed by Al Jazeera Nov 4 liveblog, Jerusalem Post, Times of Israel, TRT World, News18, Moneycontrol
fault_line: De-escalation or bluff? Trump says 'no reason' to strike while Netanyahu pushes for a strike this week — who decides the next strike, Trump or Netanyahu?

sections.what_happened: Trump told the FT the US has no immediate plans for new strikes on Iran: 'I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it.' He said 'We seem to be getting everything we want,' called the situation 'a brilliant situation,' said more oil is now passing through the Strait of Hormuz than before the war, said the US blockade is stifling Tehran's economy, said the US is 'not really in a war' with Iran, and said indirect negotiations continue over Iran's roughly 440kg (970lb) stockpile of enriched uranium ('nuclear dust'). The remarks answer Netanyahu's hints of an attack later this week; Trump declined to share attack plans in advance.
sections.what_verified: FT interview text relayed with identical quotes by AJ, JPost, ToI, TRT, News18, Moneycontrol
sections.what_disputed: Netanyahu is pushing the Trump administration for another wave of strikes on Iran after the midterms (AP, Nov 2, already recorded); Iran's SNSC Secretary Mohsen Rezaei said Nov 3 the US response to Iran's seven conditions 'was not convincing' and Hormuz reopens only when they are met (recorded 1900-02 Nov 3); Tucker Carlson's Nov 1-2 claim of a possible imminent nuclear strike on Pickaxe Mountain remains unverified and is contradicted in direction by Trump's own 'no immediate plans' line. Trump's Nov 2 Qeshm Island 'defensive' strike shows limited strikes continued even while he talked down escalation.
sections.why_matters: Claim-bust lead: Trump says no strike is needed AND that more oil flows through Hormuz than before the war — but the last counted IMF transit figure is stale (Oct 18: 4 transits). The de-escalation headline is confirmed; the oil-flow boast is not.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP + IN-WINDOW RELAY: Trump tells FT US has 'no immediate plans' to strike Iran but is 'locked and loaded' (AJ liveblog update 01:49Z = 05:49 ; fresh relays in-window)

totw_analysis: Our read: Claim-bust lead: Trump says no strike is needed AND that more oil flows through Hormuz than before the war — but the last counted IMF transit figure is stale (Oct 18: 4 transits). The de-escalation headline is confirmed; the oil-flow boast is not. The fault line our audience is arguing over: De-escalation or bluff? Trump says 'no reason' to strike while Netanyahu pushes for a strike this week — who decides the next strike, Trump or Netanyahu?
